symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the source transform, the length of the input vectors.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform of a longer length $t$, keeping both coordinate permutations inside the transform identity.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of the longer target transform, a count of its coordinates.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform of a longer length $t$, keeping both coordinate permutations inside the transform identity.

symbols.name: normalized transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized transform of length q, applied to a vector of length q.
symbols.quote: Let $F_q$ be the normalized transform of length $q$: $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}$.

symbols.name: generic linear map
symbols.meaning: A linear map whose operator norm is taken; it is a contraction when its norm is at most 1.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling is measured by the [Operator norm of a linear map](operator-norm.md), $\|L\|=\sup_{\|u\|\le1}\|Lu\|$, so a linear map $L$ is a *contraction* when $\|L\|\le1$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The integer width of the Gaussian factors, at least 2.
symbols.quote: Fix an integer width $\sigma\ge2$, the Gaussian width.

symbols.name: resampling map
symbols.meaning: The map from C^s to C^t given by the first Gaussian formula.
symbols.quote: Let $K$ and $M$ map $\mathbb C^s$ to $\mathbb C^t$ by

symbols.name: sampling map
symbols.meaning: The map from C^s to C^t given by the second Gaussian formula.
symbols.quote: Let $K$ and $M$ map $\mathbb C^s$ to $\mathbb C^t$ by

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of the source vectors with entries u_{tj}.
symbols.quote: Let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with $v$ of length $t$ (here $v$ is new).

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation of the target vectors with entries v_{-sk}.
symbols.quote: Let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with $v$ of length $t$ (here $v$ is new).

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of length t, the argument of the target permutation.
symbols.quote: Let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with $v$ of length $t$ (here $v$ is new).

symbols.name: integer precision
symbols.meaning: The integer precision of the arithmetic, the bound on the hypotheses of the theorem.
symbols.quote: The hypotheses are $p>100$, $2\le\sigma<\sqrt p$, $s<t<2^p$ and $\theta>p/\sigma^4$, where $p$ is the integer precision and $\theta=t/s-1$.

symbols.name: relative excess
symbols.meaning: The ratio t/s minus one, the relative excess of the target length over the source length.
symbols.quote: The hypotheses are $p>100$, $2\le\sigma<\sqrt p$, $s<t<2^p$ and $\theta>p/\sigma^4$, where $p$ is the integer precision and $\theta=t/s-1$.

symbols.name: nearest integer
symbols.meaning: The integer nearest tj/s, with ties rounded up.
symbols.quote: Let $\rho_j=\lfloor tj/s+\tfrac12\rfloor$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, with ties rounded up.

symbols.name: rounding offset
symbols.meaning: The offset tj/s minus its nearest integer, with absolute value at most one half.
symbols.quote: Let $\delta_j=tj/s-\rho_j$, so $|\delta_j|\le\tfrac12$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from C^t to C^s that copies coordinate rho_j into entry j.
symbols.quote: Let $\Lambda:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ select coordinate $\rho_j$, $(\Lambda v)_j=v_{\rho_j}$.

symbols.name: Gaussian diagonal
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying entry j by e^{pi sigma^2 delta_j^2}.
symbols.quote: Let $\Delta$ multiply entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\sigma^2\delta_j^2}$.

symbols.name: compensated map
symbols.meaning: The map Lambda M Delta from C^s to itself.
symbols.quote: Let $\Gamma=\Lambda M\Delta$ be the map from $\mathbb C^s$ to itself.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.
symbols.quote: The other terms form $((\Gamma-I)u)_j$, where $I$ is the identity map.

symbols.name: exponent
symbols.meaning: A positive integer with t equal to 2 to the power nu.
symbols.quote: In the application $t=2^{\nu}$, where $\nu$ is a positive integer, so $F_t$ has power-of-two length.

symbols.name: first contraction
symbols.meaning: The map one half times K, a contraction.
symbols.quote: Put $K_1=\tfrac12K$ and $K_2=2^{1-2\sigma^2}\Delta\Gamma^{-1}\Lambda$.

symbols.name: second contraction
symbols.meaning: The map 2 to the power 1 minus 2 sigma^2 times Delta Gamma^{-1} Lambda, a contraction.
symbols.quote: Put $K_1=\tfrac12K$ and $K_2=2^{1-2\sigma^2}\Delta\Gamma^{-1}\Lambda$.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform of a longer length $t$, keeping both coordinate permutations inside the transform identity.
Gaussian resampling is measured by the [Operator norm of a linear map](operator-norm.md), $\|L\|=\sup_{\|u\|\le1}\|Lu\|$, so a linear map $L$ is a *contraction* when $\|L\|\le1$.
Thus Gaussian resampling expresses each source transform through a [Multidimensional transform with power-of-two axes](multidim-transform.md).
